D'où vient la prévision ?: Where does the forecast come from?
AROME, le modèle de prévision à maille f: AROME, Météo-France's fine-mesh forecast model, computes the wind, temperature, humidity and turbulence of the air every hour, on a grid of about 2 km and on dozens of levels, from the ground to above 15 km. Four times a day (00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC runs), the site fetches these fields and derives the seeing of every hour, for each place and for the whole map.
Du modèle au seeing: From the model to the seeing
Le seeing vient de la turbulence optique: Seeing comes from optical turbulence, the Cn²: small temperature fluctuations that bend the light. It is rebuilt layer by layer, from two sources:
près du sol, dans la couche limite : la: near the ground, in the boundary layer: the turbulence computed by AROME, and convection when the ground heats up;
au-dessus : le cisaillement du vent entr: above it: the wind shear between layers, up to the jet stream.
En additionnant toutes les couches, on o: Adding up all the layers gives the seeing. This is the GmMC method of Cuevas et al. (2024).
Le seeing brut du modèle suit bien les v: The raw model seeing follows the changes from night to night well, but its level can be off:
une maille d'AROME fait environ 2 km : e: an AROME grid cell is about 2 km wide: it does not see the local effects of the terrain;
le relief y est moyenné : un sommet, un: the relief is averaged: a summit, a pass or a valley floor all get the cell's smoothed altitude;
le modèle ignore l'environnement immédia: the model knows nothing of the instrument's immediate surroundings: buildings, trees, dome, heat from the ground;
les formules qui passent de la turbulenc: the formulas going from the model's turbulence to Cn² have coefficients tuned on average, not for your site.
Le choix du modèle de turbulence compte: The choice of turbulence model matters little in the end: Cuevas et al. (2024) compared several Cn² models and, once calibrated, they give almost the same results. Calibration on measurements is what makes the difference.
On compare les prévisions passées aux me: Past forecasts are compared with the measurements of a seeing monitor, hour by hour, night after night. Two coefficients are adjusted so that the forecast matches the measurements:
K1, pour la turbulence de la couche limi: K1, for the boundary-layer turbulence (near the ground);
K2, pour la turbulence au-dessus (cisail: K2, for the turbulence above it (shear, jet stream).
Les nuits aberrantes (instrument en défa: Outlier nights (faulty instrument, clouds) can be removed. The more measured nights, and the more varied, the more reliable the calibration. The map uses a common calibration; each calibrated place has its own.
Calibrer son lieu, pas à pas: Calibrating your place, step by step

Lance le calage : K1 et K2 sont calculés: Run the calibration: K1 and K2 are computed from your nights.
Regarde la corrélation prévu / mesuré et: Look at the forecast / measured correlation and the error with the age of the run; remove doubtful nights if needed.

Carte : le seeing prévu partout, heure p: Map: the forecast seeing everywhere, hour by hour or as a night mean; part of the turbulence alone can be shown (boundary layer, altitude bands, jet stream).
Fisheye : le seeing dans chaque directio: Fisheye: the seeing in every direction of the sky from your place, with the clouds and the relief on the horizon.
Cn² : la turbulence en altitude au fil d: Cn²: the turbulence with altitude over the hours; the change from the boundary layer to the free atmosphere shows in it.
Corrélation : chaque point compare une h: Correlation: each point compares a forecast and a measured hour (or night); the closer the points to the diagonal, the better the forecast.
Erreur selon l'âge du run : la prévision: Error with the age of the run: is the forecast better a few hours ahead than two days ahead?
Seeing calculé à partir des prévisions A: Seeing computed from the AROME forecasts (Météo-France), by integrating the Cn² profile with the GmMC method (Cuevas et al. 2024), then calibrated on seeing monitor measurements. The method is explained in the tutorial.
La position sera floutée de 5 à 11 km: Position will be blurred by 5–11 km
Calcul global sur tout le domaine AROME,: Global computation over the whole AROME domain, land and sea, every 6 hours, at each main run: 00Z, 06Z, 12Z, 18Z; secondary runs are not used. The map has its own calibration, set by the administrator and refined with the measurements: it does not change with the calibration of places.
